Tornyospalca Jewish Cemetery One

Jewish Cemetery · Tornyospálca, Hungary

Not demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries in Tornyospálca, established by 1848 with tombstones through 1943. Jews lived here from 1750, including the 8-member Absolon family on the Lónyay family estate; by 1848, 100 Jews (21 families) worked as pub owners, traders, painters, butchers, rabbis, teachers, and servants, with some poorer members reduced to begging. Population peaked at 129 by 1890, settling at 76 (of 3,244 residents) by 1941, then working mostly as grocers, traders, craftsmen, and peddlers. The community joined the Orthodox stream in 1868 under Rabbi Aron Adler, maintaining a synagogue (built 1906), cheder, and Talmud Torah - before which children attended local Greek Catholic or Calvinist schools. A 2002 discovery found a white marble synagogue-wall panel hidden in a former community member's cellar after the building's demolition. Paramilitary units enforced anti-Jewish laws in 1938; in 1941, conscripted youth mostly died on the Eastern Front. In April 1944, residents were confined in the synagogue yard for two days before transfer to the Kisvárda Ghetto and deportation to Auschwitz that May, leaving only a small number of survivors.
